candidates.name: Libya–Egypt Gas Pipeline
aka: Al-Tayoub / Arab Company for Oil and Gas Pipelines (Altube) project
candidates.from: Libyan gas grid (Damietta-link variant, offshore eastern Libya); direction reversed (Egypt→Libya) in the original 2000s Altube concept

evidence.note: NOC chairman Farhat Bengdara (ADIPEC, Nov 2022): Libya studying two new gas export pipelines — one to Greece, one to Damietta in Egypt — in addition to Greenstream.

Petrojet (Egypt) and NOC (Libya) signed an MoU on 25 Jan 2026 at the Libya Energy & Economic Summit; explicitly includes studying the feasibility of transporting crude oil and natural gas between the two countries.

History of the project family: 1997 Tobruk–Sidi Krir crude line plan; 2000 $100m Egypt–Libya JV 'Altube' (Arab Company for Oil and Gas Pipelines) created to move Libyan crude to Egypt and Egyptian gas to Libya; pipelines never built.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No Egypt–Libya interconnector exists anywhere in GGIT — checked the full gas snapshot: all Libya rows (P0439, P0482–P0484, P1789, P1855–P1873, P3985–P3988, P6705–P6715 etc.) are domestic or Libya–Italy/Tunisia; no roster row touches both Egypt and Libya. Recurring project family since 1997, most recently revived by the Nov 2022 NOC Damietta study and the Jan 2026 Petrojet–NOC MoU. Still pre-feasibility/study stage with no fixed route or capacity, so it may fall below the add-threshold — flagging for the consolidator to decide.

candidates.name: Gaza Marine–El Arish Offshore Gas Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: EGAS-led consortium (EGAS 45%, operator; Palestine Investment Fund; Consolidated Contractors Company)
candidates.from: Gaza Marine gas field, offshore Gaza (Palestine), ~30-36 km off the coast
candidates.to: El Arish, Egypt (tie-in to the Egyptian gas network; swap arrangement for supplies to Idku LNG)

evidence.note: Describes the Egyptian development option: an offshore pipeline linking Gaza Marine to the Egyptian gas network at El Arish, gas swapped in-system for Idku LNG exports; EGAS MoU Feb 2021, Framework Agreement Oct 2022, Israeli preliminary approval June 2023 (Cheiron designated technical lead); all development halted by the Gaza war from Oct 2023.

Egypt/PA/Israel talks to revive Gaza Marine with EGAS as 45% operator alongside PIF (27.5%) and CCC (27.5%); gas lines would extend to the Egyptian city of Al-Arish rather than to Israel's Ashdod, with the Egyptian side processing and marketing the gas.

candidates.why_maybe_new: The only Gaza-related row in GGIT is P5276 'Gas for Gaza Pipeline' (countries = Israel only) — that is the separate Israel→Gaza supply line, opposite direction and different project. No roster row covers a Gaza Marine→Egypt export pipeline touching Egypt. This is a documented ~50-60 km subsea pipeline concept backed by signed agreements (EGAS MoU 2021, Framework Agreement 2022, Israeli preliminary approval 2023), but it is a development option tied to the stalled Gaza Marine field rather than a stand-alone sanctioned pipeline — consolidator should weigh against the add-threshold and against P5276/P3657.
